On Android, open Phone Settings → Location → Location services → Timeline → Export Timeline data. Save the file, usually named Timeline.json, somewhere easy to find. Return here and choose the file.

The exact labels can vary by phone. The button below opens Location settings; Android does not provide a standard link directly to the Timeline page.

On iPhone, use Google Maps → profile picture → Settings → Personal content → Export Timeline data.

Google Maps Timeline can remember the places you visit and the routes you travel.\n\nTimeline Visualizer turns an exported copy of that history into a private Travel Journal and animated travel videos.

Timeline Visualizer does not track your location. Your journeys must first be recorded by Google Maps Timeline.\n\nTimeline is off by default, so you need to enable it before new journeys can accumulate.
Timeline Visualizer reads only the file you choose. Your Timeline export is not uploaded to the developer.
One journey, two levels of detail

Route detail shows the point-by-point path you travelled. Journey history remembers broader visits, activities, and trips.\n\nYour Journal always uses route detail when available and Journey history as a fallback.
You do not need to choose a data mode. The app automatically uses the best information available for each part of your journey.

Recent Timeline exports often contain richer route detail. That detail may no longer appear in a later export.\n\nImport a fresh export regularly and your Journal will preserve each new detailed section on this device.
Google does not publish a guaranteed retention period for route detail. Updating every 2 to 3 weeks is a cautious recommendation based on observed exports.
Already have an export? Choose Timeline.json, location-history.json, or another supported Google Maps Timeline JSON file.
If Timeline is not enabled yet, set it up first. Google Maps can only record new journeys from that point forward.
Turn your journeys into a Travel Journal
Google Maps Timeline quietly remembers where you have been.\n\nTimeline Visualizer turns an exported copy of that history into a private Travel Journal and animated travel videos.
Timeline Visualizer does not track your location. It reads only the Timeline export you choose. Your Timeline file and Travel Journal stay on this device.
If Google Maps Timeline is not enabled, start it now to begin recording future journeys.
Export an updated Timeline.json file from Google Maps, then choose it here. Large histories may take a little longer the first time. Future imports add new detail to the same Journal.
The selected export is read locally. Its useful journey information is added to your on-device Travel Journal, and future updated exports can extend it.

Recent Timeline exports can contain detailed routes that may not appear in a later export. Importing an updated file every few weeks lets your Travel Journal preserve each new detailed stretch on this device.
Import a Google Maps Timeline export to preserve your journey history and begin building detailed routes.
